RIZZY

Brand site and simulated ordering flow for a Chicken Katsu and Es Kelapa concept.

  • StatusLive
  • CategoryProduct experience
  • Year2026
  • Stack5 technologies

Overview

RIZZY is a static brand presentation paired with a fully simulated ordering flow. A visitor can build an order, review it, and walk through a fake QRIS or USDT payment to a completed state — with no backend, no database and no money moving anywhere.

Problem

Presenting an ordering experience normally requires a working payment stack. That is expensive to build before the concept itself has been validated, so the demo had to show the full journey without pretending to be a real shop.

Approach

A browser-only demo that reproduces the ordering journey using an explicit state machine. Payment is simulated and every screen states plainly that no real order or payment occurs.

What is implemented

  • Landing page presenting the RIZZY brand and product concept.
  • Order builder: choose a package and quantity.
  • Checkout summary derived from the selected order.
  • Simulated QRIS and USDT payment screens, including explicit underpaid and overpaid states.
  • Deterministic demo state machine — status never advances on its own and never randomises.
  • Hash routing (#/, #/order, #/checkout, #/payment) so no server rewrite rules are required.
  • Safe empty states: refreshing a deep link loses the in-memory order by design instead of failing.
  • A reset control that returns the demo to an idle state.

Contribution

Public repository under Dika's GitHub account with a single-author history of 6 commits. Interface, state machine, pricing logic and demo configuration all live in one codebase.

Architecture and data flow

React 19 built with Vite. Routing is a small hash router (src/lib/hash-router.ts), which lets the build run on GitHub Pages without rewrite rules. Order state is kept in src/state/OrderContext.tsx and never leaves memory. src/lib/demo-machine.ts is a pure state machine — idle → awaiting → submitted → verified → processing → completed, with underpaid and overpaid branches — while src/lib/pricing.ts owns the totals. Catalog and payment details are configuration in src/config/. There is no backend, database, authentication, payment gateway, analytics or external API.

Stack

React 19 TypeScript Vite 8 Tailwind CSS 4 Motion for React

Verification

  • Unit tests cover the demo state machine, pricing, formatting and catalog configuration (23 test cases in source).
  • Playwright with axe-core is configured for end-to-end and accessibility checks.

Known limitations

  • Demo only — no orders are accepted and no payments are processed.
  • No backend, database or persistence; refreshing a deep link intentionally loses the order.
  • No authentication, analytics or third-party integration.
